findings.title: Caregiver alert time lacks date
findings.description: `_caregiver_message` formats heart-rate event times directly as `%H:%M` instead of using `_utc_text`, while blood-pressure messages include a date and UTC. Every non-green heart-rate alert therefore lacks a date and timezone, and a reading supplied in another timezone displays its local clock time without identifying the zone, so a caregiver may mistake an earlier event for a current one.

citations.citation: Include the date and timezone in displayed event times

print(f"Triage:     {result.triage.value.upper()}")
    print(f"Escalate:   {'yes' if result.requires_escalation else 'no'}")
    print(f"Reasons:    {'; '.join(result.reasons)}")
    print(f"To elder:   {result.message_for_elder}")
    print(f"To carer:   {result.message_for_caregiver or '-'}")
    print(f"Rules:      {result.rule_version}   Trace: {result.trace_id}")

result = HealthSentinel(load_rules(), LLMClient(provider)).assess(_hr(bpm), "tr_hr")
    assert result.triage == expected
    assert result.requires_escalation == (expected == Triage.RED)
    assert (result.message_for_caregiver is None) == (expected == Triage.GREEN)

- **Applies to:** `VitalReading.measured_at` and any text shown to an elder or caregiver that says when something happened. `measured_at` must be timezone-aware, and a naive datetime is rejected when the reading is created. A displayed time includes the date and zone, for example `2026-11-06 08:12 UTC`. New code that compares or counts time, such as the escalation service's 15-minute acknowledgement window and the daily digest, uses timezone-aware values. A change to `VitalReading` or to code that displays a time includes a test that a naive datetime is rejected and an aware one is accepted.
- **Why:** "08:12" does not say which day or which clock. A caregiver judging how urgent an alert is, and the escalation timers, both depend on knowing exactly when a reading was taken. Qodo's review of PR #1 flagged a caregiver message that showed a UTC clock time that looked like local time.
… (1 more lines)

evidence.explanation: The heart-rate branch uses `f"{reading.measured_at:%H:%M}"` rather than the date-and-UTC formatter used for blood-pressure messages, so its displayed time has neither a date nor a timezone and is not normalized to UTC. The CLI displays the caregiver message unchanged, and the amended heart-rate test checks only that a message exists rather than asserting its timestamp format.

findings.title: Health values written to logs
findings.description: `HealthSentinel.assess` passes `reading.values` and `reading.elder_id` to `logger.info` instead of using `trace_id` for correlation. On every assessment with INFO logging enabled, the measurements and elder identifier reach log handlers and aggregators, and the existing privacy test captures both.

citations.citation: Do not log health values or personal contact information
logger.info("assessed reading for %s: %s", reading.elder_id, reading.values)

        # 1. Triage is fixed here, before any model call. Nothing below can change it.
        decision = triage_reading(reading, self._rules)
        logger.info("assessed reading for %s: %s", reading.elder_id, reading.values)

result = _agent(FakeProvider(error=RuntimeError("down"))).assess(
        _bp(systolic, diastolic), "tr_1"
    )
    assert result.triage == expected
    assert result.message_for_elder == ELDER_FALLBACK[expected]
… (1 more lines)

- **Applies to:** `core/rules/`, `thresholds.yaml`, `core/baseline/`, `core/guardrail/` and `core/escalation/`. Every change adds or updates a case in `evals/` or `tests/`, including the edges (exactly at a threshold, just below it). Every threshold has an `id`, `version` and `source`. These paths need human review before merging.
- **Why:** a wrong threshold or a missed edge case is a missed alert, and any alert must be traceable to a specific rule and its source.

evidence.explanation: The added log call supplies the raw measurement dictionary and elder identifier. The existing privacy test captures INFO records and asserts that its example measurements and elder identifier are absent; repository guidance also excludes health values from logs.

findings.title: Escalation decided outside the rules
findings.description: `HealthSentinel.assess` computes `requires_escalation` using a hard-coded `bpm > 150` condition instead of relying solely on the supplied rules decision. Although the default rules already classify that range as RED, a valid rule set with a higher RED cutoff can return AMBER while the result and CLI still call for escalation that cannot be traced to a versioned rule.

citations.citation: Only the rules or baseline modules may decide triage and escalation

findings.title: Test needs live network access
findings.description: `test_can_reach_example_host` unconditionally calls `socket.create_connection` on `example.com:443` instead of testing socket behavior offline. When DNS or outbound access is unavailable, the test fails in sandboxed or offline runs, including the pull-request CI job that runs `make test`.

findings.title: A heart-rate source loses its warning
findings.description: The `hr.high` source string drops its explicit `unverified` label without any verification change in the PR. A later reader inspecting that rule sees a less qualified provenance record even though the threshold file still says its cited guidance must be verified.

citations.citation:
# Demo starting values only. Verify each against the cited guideline before relying on it.
# Every rule needs id, version, source. Rules may only name values the vital carries
# (blood_pressure: systolic, diastolic; heart_rate: bpm).

when: "systolic >= 140 or diastolic >= 90"
    triage: amber
    source: "AHA - Understanding Blood Pressure Readings (high blood pressure stage 2)"
  - id: hr.low_or_high
    version: 1
    vital: heart_rate
    when: "bpm < 40 or bpm > 130"
    triage: red
    source: "Spec section 6 - General clinical reference ranges (demo, unverified)"
  - id: hr.high
    version: 1
    vital: heart_rate
    when: "bpm > 100"
    triage: amber
    source: "Spec section 6 - resting heart rate reference range (demo)"

evidence.explanation: The changed source drops the qualifier still present on the neighboring heart-rate rule, while the file header instructs readers to verify cited guidelines before relying on these values.
